cards.adjudication: Denying the visible actor’s concern sustains it; addressing the specified empty place acknowledges a separate guest.

cards.fearMechanism: A short laugh ends in an unnaturally blank expression; the hand is treated as if the voice came through it.

cards.fearMechanism: A visible human hand is treated as a closed source of answering sound. Only the actor makes the tap.

cards.fearMechanism: The performer disowns a voice produced through their own palm and then asks about it as if they did not hear it.

cards.fearMechanism: A human reflection continues after its source stops, then acknowledges the mismatch with a delayed expression.

cards.fearMechanism: A spreading imaginary mark becomes a small tactile act; uncertainty concerns the traced pattern, not a painful or invasive prop.

collectionDecisions: The user explicitly requested a scary collection after distinguishing fear from harder difficulty. Horror is therefore collection membership, not an automatic harder label.
38 one-for-one replacements are supplied, not 38 appended missions. The complete detached editorial selection retains all six original deck counts and 147 total cards.
Shared base mechanics are intentional revisions. The base and its variant must never coexist. Within the 38-card collection each scenario has its own action and opposing outcome.
Game-facing prose is Russian; provenance and review are English. No helper field, hidden riddle explanation or empty placeholder is supplied.
Original-rule group persistence, sole-free-rescuer play, once-only rescue credit and invalidated captured-exorcist missions remain unchanged.

Paper-free scope is explicit. The earlier reference to a stationary-only performance now has the two user-authorized bounded movement scenes; they do not authorize a house-wide chase or ignoring a real stop.
Domestic revision preserves the approved 27/9/2 variant decisions. Card-level causal reasoning is linked to revision-audit.json; old paper candle and leaf scenes are replaced, not relabelled.

similarityChecks.reason: A present-room wake-up exchange differs from a reciprocal serious farewell; both use changed affect without the same release.
A ground strike and rising gesture for the below-ground walker differs from addressing an approaching figure to stop.
Identifying one independently traced shape differs from cancelling a known palm circle. A guess is not a capture condition in the mission.
